source.title: Falsehood and Impossibility Are Different Directions in an AI's Representation of Language

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different measurement—SAE encoding and class-selective activation analysis—to examine whether an LLM has recoverable sparse features. It does not test toy-model superposition itself.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the exploratory SAE feature activations. The behavioral classification, linear probes, and PCA describe coherence judgments or geometry, not superposition, polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality. No causal SAE-feature intervention was performed.
record.test_reason: The study applies a pretrained Gemma Scope 2 SAE as an analysis tool. It searches in-sample for features whose activation differs across four coherence labels on 85 prompts. It does not test whether Gemma's activations are superposed, whether features are spread across neurons, or whether an SAE recovers the model's sparse features. The mean of 10.9 active features per prompt describes the SAE checkpoint's designed sparsity, not a finding about the model. The probes and PCA bear on coherence decodability, not superposition. The reader's T2/V4 'supports' overstates the link.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that residual and SAE activity covaries with the model's coherence treatment. The probe peaks at 0.79 balanced accuracy at layer 18. They claim no unitary concept or causal mechanism, and they call the SAE features exploratory candidates.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a pretrained SAE applied to a single instruction-tuned LLM; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method or test feature-over-capacity geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE analysis is limited to layer 12 and to one model. Candidate features were selected using the same 85 prompts on which their activation was visualized.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma 3 4B IT, a few layer-12 Gemma Scope 2 SAE features show in-sample class-differential activation across coherent, contradiction, paradox, and underdetermined prompts. Several are dense and correlate with residual norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained SAE features in LLMs show label-selective activation for logical-coherence categories, though such features may reflect activation scale or surface patterns.

record.problems: One instruction-tuned 4-billion-parameter model, 85 prompts from 17 seed families, and one SAE layer. Candidate selection and visualization use the same small dataset; no independent validation or causal intervention is reported. The paper notes that several dense candidates correlate with layer-12 residual norm (absolute r up to 0.91).

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, or superposition geometry.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
No test that features are distributed across neurons or that the SAE recovers genuine sparse features. The pretrained SAE is only used as a tool.
No completeness, stability, or canonicity tests of SAE features.
No comparison of one-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked SAE candidate rows to V4 and labelled them supports and limits_scope. These rows are in-sample selection outputs of a pretrained SAE used as a tool, so they bear on no superposition version. Fig. 4 values are readable and are given in the row fixes. Several 'coherent' and 'contradiction' candidates fire on 100% of prompts and correlate with residual norm (|r| up to 0.91). This makes them weak evidence even for sparse-feature recovery. The code URL is a placeholder.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-capacity sweep, interference, sparsity-dependent transition, or superposition geometry were tested.
The study does not test capacity limits, dedicated dimensions for important features, or competition causing polysemanticity.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.

The SAE analysis is limited to one model, one layer, and the 85 study stimuli; feature selection and visualization use the same dataset. It does not validate features on an independent corpus or establish that they are semantic features.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional versus multidimensional features is made.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 4B IT
rows.operation_detail: Encoded layer-12 residual states with the Gemma Scope 2 JumpReLU SAE and measured candidate-feature activation across expected labels.

conditions.value: 85 prompts; selection and visualization on the same dataset

rows.measure: Within-feature standardized class mean log-activation and activation prevalence
rows.value: Figure 4 shows class-differential activation; the text identifies feature 477 as a coherent-associated candidate and says it is active on nearly every prompt. Exact figure values not transcribed.
rows.note: The authors describe features 477 and 514 as coherent-associated candidates with differential magnitude despite near-universal activity. Candidate status is exploratory, not a semantic identification.
rows.check: Label-selectivity of a pretrained SAE feature, selected in-sample, does not measure superposition or recoverability of sparse features. The value is readable from Fig. 4a: +1.1/-0.1/-1.6/+0.5 (coh/cont/para/unde). It is active on 100% of prompts in every class, so it is a dense, not sparse, feature.
